fields.says: A page script's second request keeps the poll's discipline: coalesce every reason into one fetch per window, and stop when the poll stops (hidden tab, 401, revoked link). `createTimelineRefresher` (`public/task-page.js`, LIN-4405) is the pattern; a running chip changes the poll's track about once a minute, so "fetch when it changes" alone repeats. Done reads once more first (`finish`): the poll that says done carries the last change, and stopping drops it.

Task-page CSS is phone-first at `min-width: 600px` (only the listed breakpoints pass `tests/unit/ui-authorities.test.js`), with `--font-size-*` tokens and no new mono selector (`tests/unit/lin-4107-type-sizes.test.js`).

`public/app.js`: Home's Running and Up next are refreshed by parsing a whole page with `DOMParser` (LIN-4243). Waiting on you is drawn as a server fragment by the page's own function (LIN-4242); doing the same for the other sections would mean the client never parses a whole page. (Survey tally: LIN-4243.)

`public/common.js`: `buildDispatchModelOptionDescriptors` repeats the merge rule of `buildModelOptions` (`lib/openrouter-catalog.js`), since the browser has no build step. The lists are not copied (they come from `window.__HARNESS_MODELS__` and the catalog over the wire); only the rule is. The endpoint could send merged options instead. (LIN-4358.)

`public/brief.js`: its `postBrief`/`errorText` block is identical to `postRecap`/`errorText` in `public/recap.js`, and the check for a `statusCode` inside a keepalive 200 body is now written four times (also `public/scan.js` and `public/observation.js`). One shared reader in `public/common.js`. (Area reads CG/CH, 8 Nov, on LIN-4358.)

`public/llms.txt`: its H11 names the unscoped `/api/recommend/status`, which is now only a legacy redirect (`routes/legacy-redirects.js`), and its view list omits `projects` and the flag-gated `live-console` (`lib/components/view-nav.js`). The browser guide is otherwise sound: its endpoints and selectors resolve. (Documentation Review, 10 Nov.; `docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-11-10.md`.)

`public/prompt-section.js`: on a server with no AI (`aiState: "unconfigured"`, a self-host with no OpenRouter key) the run control still offers Next step. Pressing it gets a 503 from the recommend stream, and "AI Recommend · generating…" / "Loading…" spin with no message, while Run to PR works beside it. Offer only what the server can do, or say why it can't. (Onboarding & Cold-Start Review, 11 Nov.; `docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-11-11.md`.)

fields.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "Side rail and other UI improvements are important purely because the current ones are just mostly the original ones and are due a bit of a sprinkling. But! The front end code is messy." And his gut: "the UI issues trace back to one of my very first rules: no build step… it's the biggest target of the Theseus method… We don't need to tidy it all, but it's a perfect example where we can leave it better than we found it. Likely this will take a fair amount of hand holding."

On main (9 Nov), no browser file can import another, nine browser files restate logic the server already has, and the largest browser file is 5,019 lines.

On the views, John: "Lots of light little views is ideal, but the cost of them has to be balanced… I'd be sad to get rid, but happy to tidy."

**What we want.**

* Browser code that shares rather than restates. There's still no build step and no framework: the rule stays, read as allowing the browser to import, as browsers do natively, and that reading goes into the project's own notes.
* Taken in small slices, one view or one shared piece at a time. Each view is reworked only after finding out why it got so large, and comes out lighter.
* Anything bigger that a slice spots is left out of it and goes into the area's note.
* The side rail and the visual refresh come after, built on the cleaner code.
* No view is retired unless John rules it.

John expects agents to reach for big moves here: "very likely to get agents trying really hard to do big things when we want small." So the size is John's call, and for this work it's small.

**Done when** the reading of the rule is in the project's notes; the first slice has landed, sharing rather than restating, lighter than before and naming what it retired; and John has read the first slice's result before the next starts.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.
fields.done-when: the reading of the rule is in the project's notes; the first slice has landed, sharing rather than restating, lighter than before and naming what it retired; and John has read the first slice's result before the next starts.

fields.says: "Allow the browser to import" does not turn imports on: `server.js:1228` serves only `public/`, so the server modules a browser file restates (`lib/cost-format.js` etc.) have no URL. Sharing needs a served place for pure modules that both `lib/` and the browser import, plus a written rule for it (no Node built-ins, no DOM at load), or someone will import a module that pulls in `node:fs`. CSP `script-src 'self'` already allows module scripts loaded from a file. (Survey @ 4b5001ddf.)

fields.says: Every page is classic scripts talking through globals: `lib/components/page.js` writes ordered `<script src>` tags, and files read `window.X` and top-level bindings from `public/common.js` (3,309 lines, on 29 pages). A classic script cannot use static `import`; making a view `type="module"` makes it deferred, strict and module-scoped, so its globals vanish for later scripts. "One view at a time" is blocked until what views read from `common.js` is reachable another way. Bigger than a slice: kept out of LIN-4446's first slice, as is view size. (Survey @ 4b5001ddf.)

The unit harness assumes classic scripts: 130 test files load `public/*.js` through `vm` (`tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js`, plus `runInNewContext` in the parity tests); none use `vm.SourceTextModule`. A browser file that gains an `import` line breaks all of them. That cost is not in the ticket; a slice must keep the files it touches loadable by the vm suites or give them a module path. (Survey @ 4b5001ddf.)

fields.says: State of the place (survey @ 4b5001ddf): `public/` is 79 files, 35,264 lines of JS, all classic scripts sharing through `window.*` globals in the order each `lib/render-*.js` lists in `scripts: [...]`. `common.js` (3,309 lines, 56 `window.` assignments) already calls itself the "client twin" of `lib/task-page-href.js`, `lib/timeline-zoom.js`, `lib/ship-layout.js` and `lib/prompt-formatters.js`; `swim.js` copies `lib/swim-lanes.js`. Growth 15.4k lines (1 Jul) → 29.1k (1 Oct) → 35.1k (9 Nov): about 1,200 a week in October, about 300 a week since 1 Nov; `observation.js` has held near 5,000 since mid-October. Stopped getting worse, not yet getting better. After cost-format, the next leaf twins of the same shape are `task-page-href` and `timeline-zoom` (zero imports).

The comment count in finding-14 does not match mine: I count 1,006 comment lines out of 4,679 non-blank in `public/observation.js` (mostly logic), against finding-14's ~1,985 of 5,019. Before judging "lighter" on logic and commentary counted separately, settle one counting method (blank lines, block vs line comments, JSDoc) and state it in the verdict. (Survey place @ 4b5001ddf.)

The weight sits in the tests: 126 unit suites by my count run `public/` scripts through `vm` (`tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js`, `loadWorld`), so the harness enforces "no imports" as much as the browser does, and converting a view to a module drags its whole suite family with it (the big move John warns of). Order for the work beyond LIN-4446's first slice: (1) a module-capable client-test loader (`vm.SourceTextModule` or equivalent), its own slice, before any view becomes a module; (2) then breaking up `common.js`'s globals; (3) then finding out why `observation.js` is as large as it is. The keepalive `statusCode` readers (finding-6) and `buildDispatchModelOptionDescriptors` (finding-5) belong to that work. (Survey place @ 4b5001ddf.)

Where shared modules are served: not a second `express.static('lib')`, which would expose all server source. `lib/vendor-assets.js` is already a frozen URL→file allow-list that runs `statSync` at boot, so a missing file fails the boot. Extend it for shared modules and there stays one way to serve files from outside `public/`. CSP already admits same-origin modules. (Survey place @ 4b5001ddf.)

fields.says:
Share lib/cost-format.js with the browser, retire its restated copy, then stop for John. Re-grounded at 4b5001ddf: no commits since 12:08 on any named path. Fits one session; plan-review due.

Which way. (a) Serve through the allow-list: a second frozen map SHARED_MODULES in lib/vendor-assets.js (/shared/cost-format.js -> lib/cost-format.js), statSync at boot, with a rootDir option for tests; VENDOR_ASSETS untouched (vendor-assets.test.js pins its three URLs); mount stays just before express.static('public'). Set aside: express.static('lib') (publishes all server source); moving the file into public/ (lib/render-*.js would import from the web root). (b) Bridge with a deferred module shim public/cost-format-global.js that imports formatUsd and sets window.CostFormat; no view becomes a module, common.js and the vm loaders untouched. Set aside: converting a consumer (needs a module-capable test loader); keeping public/cost-format.js as a wrapper.
